stories.title: Nvidia tones down DLSS 5 for its Hogwarts Legacy debut next month
stories.summary: Nvidia has scaled back its AI-driven DLSS 5 upscaling for its debut in Hogwarts Legacy next month, after earlier demos drew criticism for visibly altering character faces.
stories.more: When Nvidia first showed DLSS 5 earlier this year, the technology was quickly branded as generative AI for video games, and reaction among gamers was negative. Early demonstrations showed the tool visibly transforming faces, including making a 15-year-old Hogwarts Legacy student look noticeably older and altering a character from Resident Evil. Nvidia has now toned down the effect ahead of DLSS 5's debut in Hogwarts Legacy next month. Specific technical changes behind the toned-down version were not detailed in available reporting.

stories.title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy five years after launch
stories.summary: Character.AI has filed for bankruptcy and will sell some assets to Disney for $20 million, with the platform shutting down entirely if no buyer is found.
stories.more: Character.AI, the interactive chatbot platform founded by ex-Google researchers, has filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. The company will sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million as part of the process. If no other buyer emerges, the platform will shut down entirely; a sale is expected to close by the end of 2026. Character.AI once had over 20 million users but had been battling lawsuits over harm to minors and operational problems. The company's trajectory marks a steep fall from a $2.7 billion Google deal.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon, its new frontier reasoning model
stories.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Argon, claiming frontier-level reasoning and reduced hedging and repetition, with a paid rollout in the Gemini app and Antigravity and discounted API rates through November.
stories.more: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon after months on the sidelines of the frontier AI race, positioning it to compete with the industry's best models. The company says Argon delivers frontier reasoning and improved performance on complex workflows while cutting down on hedging, repetition, and clichéd phrasing common in earlier models. DeepMind published a companion blog post covering the model's use in robotics alongside the main launch announcement. The model is rolling out in the Gemini app and in Antigravity, but access requires a paid subscription, and developers get a 50 percent discount on API rates through November. The launch drew significant discussion on Hacker News, with over 200 points and more than 160 comments.

stories.title: Fields medalists warn AI proofs dumb down math as China builds alliance
stories.summary: 25 Western Fields Medal winners are warning against AI-generated proofs, with some pushing for a boycott, as China launches a 1,000-scientist alliance to push AI into math research.
stories.more: In the West, 25 Fields Medal winners have warned that AI-generated proofs risk making mathematicians less capable, with parts of the community calling for an outright boycott of such tools. China is moving in the opposite direction: Fields Medal winner Shing-Tung Yau has launched an alliance of eight institutions and more than 1,000 scientists dedicated to pushing AI into mathematical research. The split illustrates a broader divide in how different parts of the global math community are responding to AI's growing role in proof-writing and discovery.

stories.title: GroundAnything replaces autoregressive visual grounding with parallel diffusion
stories.summary: A new paper proposes bidirectional diffusion for visual grounding, letting spatial predictions emerge in parallel instead of token-by-token, aiming for faster, more accurate results.
stories.more: The paper argues that autoregressive grounding models serialize spatial predictions, adding sequential latency and forcing an artificial left-to-right order on outputs. The authors reframe grounding as visual evidence extraction, where objects, locations, and spatial relations are jointly constrained by the image and query rather than generated in sequence. This framing motivates a bidirectional diffusion approach that lets spatial hypotheses emerge in parallel and be refined jointly. The method is presented under the name GroundAnything, targeting what the authors call 'flash speed' grounding. The available excerpt does not specify benchmark results or release details.

items.title: GroundAnything: Reconciling Parallel Decoding with Precise Visual Grounding at Flash Speed
items.excerpt: Autoregressive (AR) grounding models serialize spatial predictions, introducing sequential latency and imposing a causal order on output tokens. We view grounding as visual evidence extraction: objects, locations, and spatial relations are jointly constrained by the image and query, yet their dependencies do not imply an intrinsic left-to-right generation order. This distinction makes bidirectional diffusion a natural fit, allowing spatial hypotheses to emerge in parallel and be jointly refined

stories.title: Geoffrey Huntley: pre-commit hooks can steer coding agents mid-task
stories.summary: In a quoted post, developer Geoffrey Huntley describes using a pre-commit hook that fails a commit and injects a prompt telling a coding agent to use his diagnostics library instead of bypassing it.
stories.more: The quote, shared via Simon Willison's blog, comes from developer Geoffrey Huntley discussing how he keeps AI coding agents aligned with his preferred tooling. Rather than relying on agents to read and follow instructions in a file like AGENTS.md, which can drift out of date, Huntley writes a pre-commit hook that checks the git diff for direct calls to observability modules that bypass his diagnostics library. When it finds a violation, the hook fails the commit and injects a prompt telling the agent to use the diagnostics library instead. Huntley says this approach reliably fixes the agent's behavior, calling the result 'ten out of ten.'

items.title: Quoting Geoffrey Huntley
items.excerpt: If the agent isn't using my diagnostics library, I could introspect and update AGENTS.md, but there's still a delta, and it'll drift. Instead, I write a pre-commit hook that checks the git diff for direct calls to observability modules that bypass my diagnostics module. Boom: fail the commit, inject a prompt telling the agent to use the diagnostics library. All of a sudden it's ten out of ten. — Geoffrey Huntley , nobody should type code by hand anymore. here's what's left. Tags: coding-agents ,

stories.title: Mia Goth calls viral AI deepfake of her on Instagram 'incomprehensible'
stories.summary: Actress Mia Goth said it was 'incomprehensible' that Instagram let a verified account spread an AI-generated image of her wearing a shirt mocking her ex, Shia LaBeouf.
stories.more: The controversy follows news that Goth had filed for divorce from actor and filmmaker Shia LaBeouf. A verified Instagram account, miagoth_, posted an AI-generated image showing Goth in a T-shirt reading 'MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN.' The post spread quickly despite not being from Goth's real account. Goth publicly objected to Instagram allowing the fake, verified post to circulate. It is unclear from available reporting what action, if any, Instagram has taken on the account.

stories.title: War game on dimming the Sun shows geopolitics making it worse
stories.summary: A simulation that war-gamed solar geoengineering, deliberately dimming sunlight to offset warming, found outcomes worsen once geopolitics gets involved.
stories.more: Researchers ran a simulation war-gaming solar geoengineering, the idea of deliberately dimming sunlight to counter global warming. The exercise modeled what happens once geopolitical dynamics enter the picture. According to the report, outcomes turned out worse than expected once different nations' competing interests were factored in. Specific countries, policy proposals, or numerical outcomes from the simulation were not detailed in the available excerpt.
